title: Region readiness aggregator and probabilistic warm-standby prefill playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Implement a lightweight Region Readiness Aggregator service and an associated playbook that drives probabilistic warm-standby prefill (KV and prefix cache) and tier-aware routing adjustments during degradation. The goal is to reduce cold-cache latency spikes during region cutovers while keeping prefill cost bounded by using dynamic sampling and regional scoring.

Scope:
- Readiness Aggregator: a read-only stream processor that ingests health telemetry (latency p50/p95, token throughput, active model variants, recent failover events) and outputs a per-region readiness score and confidence window.
- Prefill Orchestrator: component that consumes scores and issues targeted KV cache snapshot prefill or lightweight probe traffic at controlled rates.
- Policy engine: maps readiness score + tier (free/standard/enterprise) to prefill intensity, allowed fallback variants, and routing weight shifts.
- Playbook & Runbook: guidance for SREs on manual escalation, rollback thresholds, and simulated rehearsals.

Key decisions and trade-offs so far:
- Use probabilistic sampling rather than deterministic prefill to cap cross-region GPU egress and cold-start cost. We sample requests by user cohort and route a fraction of shadow traffic to standby region to both exercise caches and validate model variant compatibility.
- Readiness score is intentionally interpretable (0-100) using three signals: cache hit trend, p95 latency delta versus baseline, and sustained availability flags. We avoid opaque ML models to keep on-call debugging straightforward.
- KV snapshot frequency will be tiered: Enterprise (daily delta snapshots), Standard (weekly rolling snapshots), Free (on-demand probes only). This balances cost vs. SLAs.
- Prefill vs. full model deploy: initial implementation only seeds KV and prefix caches; full model variant sync is out of scope and will be gated behind separate rollout.

Work completed:
- Aggregator design doc drafted and linked below.
- Prototype readiness scorer implemented as a Flink job with synthetic telemetry; validated on canary cluster.
- Prefill Orchestrator PoC that triggers small (0.5-2% traffic) shadow probes to target region implemented behind feature flag.

Open risks:
- Over-prefilling may exhaust standby capacity in tightly provisioned Dedicated pools; need autoscaling/quotas integration.
- Model variant incompatibility when fallback variant is older/quantized; must ensure semantic compatibility or include automatic sanitization layer.

Next steps:
- Integrate Aggregator output into routing controller to enable gradual traffic weight shifts (canary-style) when readiness > 80 and confidence window stable for 5 minutes.
- Add cost-safety guardrails: global prefill budget per-account and per-region throttle.
- Implement acceptance tests: staged shadow rehearsal, chaos-simulated latency injection, and validation against token-rate billing dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
- Readiness score computed and persisted for all regions within 30s of telemetry ingestion.
- Prefill orchestrator can seed KV snapshots for given region at configured sampling rates and respect per-account budget throttles.
- Routing controller can perform a gradual 0->10% traffic shift to standby region automatically when readiness policy conditions are met, and roll back on regressions.
